the FUEL framework is a useful model for understanding listening effort and its effects on auditory and cognitive functioning, and that social psychological factors can be incorporated into the framework to better predict listening effort.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FUEL framework can be extended to include social factors that affect listeners’ self-perceptions and motivations to engage in challenging listening situations.
listening effort is not only about the listener’s actual abilities but also about the listener’s perception and evaluation of their abilities and their motivation to expend effort.

listening is an active process, and that the listener’s appraisal of the listening situation, and of his or her capacity to meet the demands of the situation, are important determinants of the amount of listening effort that the listener will expend.
